newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end sharply down after baht plunge.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end sharply down after baht plunge.

text.p: Thai stocks tumbled 3.20 percent at the close on Friday on mounting worries about listed companies' foreign exchange losses following the baht's steep fall, brokers said.
The composite SET index ended down 20.78 points at 628.55 on 7.08 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index dropped 2.07 points to 47.12.
"The baht's sharp drop today would certainly widen companies' foreign exchange loss. This made us revise down further their earnings projection," said one broker Ekachart Finance and Securities.

The Thai baht tumbled to new record low of 30.03 to the dollar in mid-afternoon trade on Friday largely affected by spillover negative sentiment from events gripping the Philippine peso, dealers said.
Brokers also said rumours that some small-sized banks faced liquidity problems also dampened market sentiment.
Selling pressure focused on bank and communications shares, while speculative buying in some finance shares weighed down the market loss, brokers said.
Finance buying was focused on stocks of five large Thai finance and securities firms leading consolidations of weaker firms in the troubled industry, brokers said.
Thai Farmers Bank fell four baht to 105 on the most active trade of 332 million baht.
Bangkok Bank tumbled 12 to 162 and Krung Thai Bank dipped 1.75 to 34. National Finance was up one to 28.75.
